title: Properties of Simple Covalent Compounds - Worksheet 2
topic: Structure, Bonding and Physical Properties of Simple Covalent Molecules
subject: Pure Chemistry

questions.question: Which statement correctly explains why simple covalent molecules have low melting points?
options: Weak covalent bonds within the molecules
Weak intermolecular forces between the molecules
Strong electrostatic forces between ions
Delocalised electrons between molecules
questions.explanation: Simple covalent molecules have strong covalent bonds within each molecule, but weak intermolecular forces between separate molecules. Little energy is needed to overcome these weak forces, resulting in low melting and boiling points.

questions.question: Why does carbon dioxide not conduct electricity in any state?
options: It contains no charged particles
It has no mobile ions or delocalised electrons
Its molecules are too small to carry charge
It is a gas at room temperature
questions.explanation: Simple covalent molecules like CO₂ have all electrons involved in covalent bonds or as lone pairs. There are no free electrons or mobile ions to carry electric charge, so they do not conduct electricity in solid, liquid or gaseous states.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: The weak forces of attraction between simple covalent molecules are called ______.
options: covalent bonds
ionic bonds
intermolecular forces
metallic bonds
questions.explanation: Intermolecular forces are the weak forces of attraction between separate molecules. These are much weaker than the covalent bonds within molecules and are easily overcome during melting or boiling.

questions.question: Which substance is most likely to be a simple covalent molecule?
options: A solid with high melting point that conducts electricity when molten
A liquid with low boiling point that does not conduct electricity
A solid that is malleable and conducts electricity
A solid with very high melting point that does not conduct electricity
questions.explanation: Simple covalent molecules typically have low melting/boiling points due to weak intermolecular forces, and do not conduct electricity because they lack mobile charged particles.

questions.question: Why does iodine sublime easily when heated?
options: The covalent bonds within I₂ molecules break easily
The weak intermolecular forces between I₂ molecules are easily overcome
Iodine molecules decompose into atoms when heated
Iodine has metallic bonding that allows easy vaporisation
questions.explanation: Iodine exists as I₂ molecules held together by weak intermolecular forces. These forces require little energy to overcome, allowing iodine to sublime (change directly from solid to gas) with gentle heating. The strong covalent bonds within I₂ molecules remain intact.

questions.question: Complete the explanation: Water has a low boiling point because the ______ between water molecules require little energy to overcome.
options: covalent bonds
electrostatic forces
intermolecular forces
metallic bonds
questions.explanation: Water is a simple covalent molecule. The molecules are held together by weak intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds), which require little energy to overcome during boiling. The strong covalent bonds within water molecules remain intact.

questions.question: Which statement about the structure of simple covalent substances is correct?
options: They consist of giant lattices of atoms
They consist of discrete molecules with weak forces between them
They consist of positive ions in a sea of electrons
They consist of oppositely charged ions in a regular pattern
questions.explanation: Simple covalent substances consist of discrete molecules. Strong covalent bonds hold atoms together within each molecule, but weak intermolecular forces exist between separate molecules.

questions.question: Why does methane (CH₄) not dissolve in water but dissolves in hexane?
options: Methane molecules are too large to fit between water molecules
Methane is non-polar while water is polar; like dissolves like
Methane reacts with water to form a gas
Hexane has stronger intermolecular forces than water
questions.explanation: Methane is a non-polar simple covalent molecule. Water is polar. 'Like dissolves like' - non-polar substances dissolve better in non-polar solvents like hexane than in polar solvents like water.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: The strong bonds within a simple covalent molecule are called ______ bonds.
options: ionic
metallic
covalent
intermolecular
questions.explanation: Covalent bonds are the strong bonds formed by sharing electron pairs between atoms within a molecule. These are much stronger than the weak intermolecular forces between separate molecules.

questions.question: Which property is NOT typical of simple covalent molecules?
options: Low melting and boiling points
Do not conduct electricity
Often soluble in organic solvents
High electrical conductivity when molten
questions.explanation: Simple covalent molecules do not conduct electricity in any state because they contain no mobile charged particles. High conductivity when molten is a property of ionic compounds, not simple covalent molecules.

questions.question: Why does ethanol (C₂H₅OH) have a higher boiling point than methane (CH₄)?
options: Ethanol has stronger covalent bonds within its molecules
Ethanol molecules have stronger intermolecular forces than methane molecules
Ethanol is an ionic compound while methane is covalent
Ethanol molecules are smaller than methane molecules
questions.explanation: Ethanol molecules can form hydrogen bonds (a type of intermolecular force) due to the O-H group. Methane only has weak London dispersion forces. Stronger intermolecular forces in ethanol require more energy to overcome, giving a higher boiling point.

questions.question: Complete the explanation: Simple covalent substances are often gases or liquids at room temperature because the ______ between molecules are weak and easily overcome.
options: covalent bonds
electrostatic forces
intermolecular forces
metallic bonds
questions.explanation: The weak intermolecular forces between simple covalent molecules require little energy to overcome. This allows the molecules to separate easily, resulting in low melting/boiling points and often gaseous or liquid states at room temperature.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the forces in iodine (I₂) and sodium chloride (NaCl)?
options: Both have strong covalent bonds between atoms
I₂ has weak intermolecular forces; NaCl has strong electrostatic forces between ions
Both have weak intermolecular forces between molecules
I₂ has strong ionic bonds; NaCl has weak covalent bonds
questions.explanation: Iodine is a simple covalent molecule with weak intermolecular forces between I₂ molecules. Sodium chloride is an ionic compound with strong electrostatic forces between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in a giant lattice.

questions.question: Why does solid iodine not conduct electricity?
options: It contains no charged particles
Its molecules have no mobile ions or delocalised electrons
Its covalent bonds are too strong to allow electron flow
It is a non-metal and all non-metals are insulators
questions.explanation: Iodine consists of I₂ molecules with all electrons involved in covalent bonds or as lone pairs. There are no free electrons or mobile ions to carry electric charge, so solid iodine does not conduct electricity.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: When a simple covalent substance melts, the ______ between molecules are overcome, but the ______ within molecules remain intact.
options: covalent bonds, intermolecular forces
intermolecular forces, covalent bonds
ionic bonds, covalent bonds
metallic bonds, ionic bonds
questions.explanation: Melting a simple covalent substance only requires overcoming the weak intermolecular forces between molecules. The strong covalent bonds within each molecule remain intact during melting or boiling.

questions.question: Which observation suggests a substance is made of simple covalent molecules?
options: It has a high melting point and conducts electricity when molten
It has a low melting point and does not conduct electricity
It is malleable and conducts electricity in solid state
It has a very high melting point and is hard and brittle
questions.explanation: Simple covalent molecules typically have low melting/boiling points due to weak intermolecular forces, and do not conduct electricity because they lack mobile charged particles.

questions.question: Why does hydrogen chloride (HCl) gas dissolve in water to form an acidic solution?
options: HCl molecules break into H⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in water
HCl molecules react with water to form ions
HCl is an ionic compound that dissociates in water
Water molecules break the covalent bonds in HCl
questions.explanation: HCl is a simple covalent molecule. When it dissolves in water, the polar water molecules interact with HCl, causing it to ionise: HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻. This produces H⁺(aq) ions, making the solution acidic.

questions.question: Complete the explanation: Simple covalent molecules do not conduct electricity because all electrons are ______ in covalent bonds or as lone pairs.
options: delocalised
transferred
localised
ionised
questions.explanation: In simple covalent molecules, all valence electrons are either shared in covalent bonds between atoms or exist as lone pairs on atoms. There are no free or delocalised electrons to carry electric charge.

questions.question: Which pair of substances are both simple covalent molecules?
options: Sodium chloride and water
Carbon dioxide and methane
Magnesium oxide and ammonia
Iron and sulfur
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) and methane (CH₄) are both simple covalent molecules. They consist of discrete molecules held by weak intermolecular forces, with strong covalent bonds within each molecule.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: The physical properties of simple covalent substances depend mainly on the strength of the ______ between molecules.
options: covalent bonds
ionic bonds
intermolecular forces
metallic bonds
questions.explanation: The physical properties (melting point, boiling point, solubility) of simple covalent substances depend on the strength of intermolecular forces between molecules. The strong covalent bonds within molecules affect chemical properties, not physical properties like melting point.
